guard: the lifecycle hook relay fails OPEN on a configuration fault without failing SILENT, and does not warn about a session that legitimately has no control plane
why: THE DEFECT WAS SILENCE, NOT FAILURE, so a mutation that breaks the relay outright proves nothing
about this repair. Both mutations below leave the relay working and change only what it says.
M1 restores the shipped behaviour exactly: the catch still fails open, and now says nothing. The
operator's symptom is a seat whose presence never advances and which never receives a queued peer
message, with no line anywhere to read. R1 is the assertion that refuses to accept that as
success. This is the same class the hermes Python hooks shipped, one connector over, which is why
the repair is a warning and not a stricter refusal.
M2 IS THE OTHER HALF AND IT MATTERS AS MUCH. Moving the warning to the no-control branch makes
the relay warn on every hook of a legitimate hand-driven session that never had a control socket.
A warning channel that fires on working configurations is trained into background noise inside a
day, at which point the R1 warning is present and unread, which is indistinguishable from the
defect. R3 is the assertion that keeps the discrimination honest.
BUILD FIRST because the relay resolves through dist/, and afterRestore rebuilds because dist/ is
gitignored and git cannot be the recovery for a tree holding a build compiled from the mutant.

mutations.name: M1 the relay fails open silently again
mutations.find:
function warnOnce(message: string): void {

mutations.replace:

mutations.expectRed: R1: a hook whose control endpoint cannot be resolved says so on stderr
mutations.note: The shipped defect restored. R1's sibling assertions (exit 0, empty stdout) stay green under it, which is the point: the broken build looked healthy on every path anyone was watching.

mutations.name: M2 the relay warns about a session that simply has no control plane
mutations.expectRed: R3: a session with no control endpoint at all is not warned about
mutations.note: Over-warning is the failure mode that destroys the value of the fix without breaking a single functional assertion. A hand-driven session sets COTAL_NAME and has no control socket; under this mutant it is told it is broken on every lifecycle event.
